title: Progressive Wealth Taxation
by: Emmanuel Saez and Gabriel Zucman
summary: Brookings Papers on Economic Activity paper on the revenue potential, enforcement and economic effects of a tax on the wealth of the richest US families, with lessons from other countries.

title: A blueprint for a coordinated minimum effective taxation standard for ultra-high-net-worth individuals
by: Gabriel Zucman, for the Brazilian G20 presidency (EU Tax Observatory)
summary: Commissioned by the G20 presidency: proposes a minimum tax of 2% of wealth a year for individuals worth over $1 billion, which countries could levy as a wealth tax or by other means.

title: A wealth tax for the UK: final report
by: Wealth Tax Commission (Arun Advani, Emma Chamberlain, Andy Summers)
summary: Independent commission (LSE, Warwick and a tax barrister) concluding that a one-off wealth tax is the better choice if the government wants to raise more revenue from wealth.

title: Ultra-Millionaire Tax Act
by: Sen. Elizabeth Warren, Reps. Brendan Boyle and Pramila Jayapal
status: Introduced
summary: A yearly 2% tax on net worth between $50 million and $1 billion and 3% above $1 billion, with a 40% exit tax on those who renounce citizenship. Reintroduced in later Congresses.

title: Proposition de loi n° 768 instaurant un impôt plancher de 2 % sur le patrimoine des ultra riches
by: Eva Sas, Clémentine Autain and the Écologiste et Social group
status: Passed the Assemblée nationale in February 2025; not adopted by the Sénat on 12 June 2025
summary: The "taxe Zucman": a floor tax of 2% on the wealth of the richest households.

title: Antrag 21/4029: Vermögensteuer wieder erheben – Länderfinanzen nachhaltig sichern
by: Fraktion Die Linke
status: First reading on 6 March 2026, referred to the Finance Committee; its report (Drucksache 21/8481, 9 October 2026) recommends rejecting the motion, with CDU/CSU, AfD, SPD and Greens against Die Linke
summary: Asks the government to bring in a bill that levies the wealth tax again: a net wealth tax from 1% above 1 million euro, rising to 5% at 50 million and 12% above 1 billion.

title: Ley 38/2022: Impuesto Temporal de Solidaridad de las Grandes Fortunas
by: Cortes Generales
status: In force
summary: Created a state-level tax on net wealth above €3 million, with rates from 0% to 3.5%, on top of the regional wealth tax.

title: Wealth Inequality and Closing the Poverty Gap in Arab Countries: The Case for a Solidarity Wealth Tax
by: Khalid Abu-Ismail and Vladimir Hlasny, UN ESCWA
summary: A UN ESCWA technical paper estimating that a solidarity wealth tax on the richest tenth of adults, about 1.2% a year in the middle-income Arab countries, could cover the cost of closing the poverty gap there; the least developed countries would need outside help.

title: Commitment to Reducing Inequality Index: Malawi Country Profile 2025
by: Jo Walker and Matthew Martin (with Oxfam in Malawi, MEJN, and NCA-DCA)
summary: Evaluates Malawi's fiscal framework and inequality gap, recommending a moderate wealth tax of 0.7% on accumulated wealth (raising ~$70M) to fund universal essential healthcare for 890,000 citizens.

title: Motion 20.3174: Millionäre besteuern, um Gemeinwesen zu finanzieren und Arbeitsplätze zu retten
by: Denis de la Reussille (Swiss Party of Labour)
status: Rejected by the National Council on 22 September 2021 (65 yes, 118 no)
summary: Asks the Federal Council to introduce a Covid-19 solidarity tax on wealth over CHF 3 million and use the proceeds for workers, families and small businesses.

title: Motion 20.3203: Solidaritätsabgabe auf Milliardenvermögen zur Bekämpfung der Corona-Krise
by: Social Democratic group (SP)
status: Rejected by the National Council on 15 March 2022 (66 yes, 126 no)
summary: Asks the Federal Council to set up a Covid-19 fund financed by a temporary solidarity levy on wealth of CHF 1 billion and above.

title: Motion 23.3361: Für eine Steuer auf dem Vermögen der Superreichen!
by: Stefania Prezioso Batou (Ensemble à Gauche)
status: Rejected by the National Council on 13 March 2024 (60 yes, 132 no)
summary: Asks the Federal Council to amend Article 128 of the Federal Constitution so that a direct federal tax on the wealth of natural persons can be levied.

title: Vote 22 (43rd Parliament, 2nd Session): opposition motion for a new 1% tax on wealth over $20 million
by: Peter Julian (NDP)
summary: Opposition motion asking the government to put in place a new one percent tax on wealth over $20 million and an excess profit tax on big corporations, and to spend the proceeds on income security, health care and housing.
status: Negatived on 16 November 2020, 27 yeas to 292 nays (the House of Commons vote record)

title: Motion M-43: Wealth tax
by: Peter Julian (NDP), seconded by Gord Johns and Alistair MacGregor
summary: Private member's motion: "the government should immediately implement a 1% wealth tax on fortunes over $20 million".
status: Reinstated from the previous session on 23 September 2020; the page shows no debate or vote. The 43rd Parliament has since ended.

title: Motion M-68: Wealth inequality
by: Nathaniel Erskine-Smith (Liberal), seconded by Paul Manly and Elizabeth May
summary: Private member's motion asking the government to levy a one-time tax on extreme wealth to help pay for the pandemic response (3% on assets over $10 million, 5% over $20 million), alongside an inheritance tax on estates over $5 million and a fairer tax treatment of investment income.
status: Placed on notice on 11 February 2021; the page shows no later activity. The 43rd Parliament has since ended.

title: Net wealth tax on Canadian resident economic families
by: Nigel Wodrich, Parliamentary Budget Officer, at the request of Peter Julian MP
summary: Official costing of an annual tax of 1% on family net wealth above $20 million: the PBO estimates 13,800 families would pay it and that it would raise $5.6 billion net in 2020-21.

title: Implementing annual wealth tax (45th General Election costing)
by: Parliamentary Budget Officer, for the New Democratic Party
summary: Election costing of the NDP's annual household wealth tax (1% on net worth from $10 million to $50 million, 2% to $100 million, 3% above): about $22.8 billion net in 2025-26 and $121.3 billion over five years, assuming 35% of each household's wealth is hidden.

title: Multi-Millionaires and Fair Taxes: The Case for a Wealth Tax in Canada
by: Andrew Jackson (Broadbent Institute), edited by Katrina Miller
summary: Argues for an annual wealth tax to help pay for the pandemic, reviews the NDP's 2019 proposal of 1% above $20 million and the practical objections, and concludes that it is a feasible political choice.

title: Report: It's Time To Tax Extreme Wealth Inequality
by: Toby Sanger and Erika Beauchesne (Canadians for Tax Fairness)
summary: Proposes a graduated annual wealth tax of 1% above $10 million, 2% above $100 million and 3% above $1 billion, which it estimates would raise close to $20 billion a year.

title: Un nouvel impôt sur le patrimoine
by: Guillaume Hébert (IRIS)
summary: Proposes a Québec tax on household net assets above $2 million, at 0.2% from $2 to 5 million, 0.5% to $25 million, 0.75% to $100 million and 1.25% above, aimed at the richest 10% of households and estimated to raise about $6.8 billion.

title: Proposición de Ley 122/000213: Impuesto sobre la titularidad, tenencia, disponibilidad, disfrute o uso de bienes o derechos por personas con grandes fortunas
by: Grupo Parlamentario Confederal de Unidas Podemos-En Comú Podem-Galicia en Común
summary: Would create a tax on the net wealth of people with large fortunes (from EUR 10 million), with an eight-bracket scale of marginal rates from 3.6% to 5% on total net wealth after debts and a EUR 1 million reduction of the base.
status: Rechazada (the Pleno of the Congreso debated its taking into consideration and rejected it, 7 June 2022)

title: Proposición de Ley 122/000045: Impuesto sobre la titularidad, tenencia, disponibilidad, disfrute o uso de bienes o derechos por personas con grandes fortunas
by: Grupo Parlamentario Mixto (Podemos deputies)
summary: Re-presents the Podemos bill for a tax on the net wealth of people with large fortunes, with the same eight-bracket scale of marginal rates from 3.6% to 5% and a EUR 1 million reduction of the base.
status: Admitida a trámite por la Mesa del Congreso (9 January 2024); published in the BOCG on 12 January 2024

title: Proposición de Ley 122/000303: creación del Gravamen sobre la Concentración de Riqueza
by: Grupo Parlamentario Plurinacional SUMAR
summary: Would levy a single 3% rate each year on the part of a person's net wealth above EUR 50 million, and cap the marginal rate of the Impuesto sobre el Patrimonio at 3.5% on that part.
status: Admitida a trámite por la Mesa de la Cámara (22 September 2026)

title: Norma Foral 23/2023, de 15 de diciembre, por la que se regula el Impuesto Temporal de Solidaridad de las Grandes Fortunas (Álava)
by: Juntas Generales de Álava
summary: Regulates in Álava the temporary solidarity tax on large fortunes, a complement to the wealth tax that applies to net wealth above EUR 3,000,000.
status: Approved by the Juntas Generales de Álava on 15 December 2023; published in the BOTHA no. 150 of 29 December 2023

title: Un Tope a la Riqueza para España: Evidencia sobre su Potencial Impacto
by: Marina Alcázar, Olga Cantó and Francisco García-Rodríguez (The Wealth Cap Project)
summary: Finds that Spain's billionaires pay an effective rate of about 0.09% of their wealth through the Impuesto sobre el Patrimonio and the solidarity tax, and estimates that a wealth cap could raise about EUR 50.3 billion.

title: Un impuesto al patrimonio para el siglo XXI: opciones para rediseñar el IP y recaudar más de los que más tienen
by: Íñigo Macías Aymar (Oxfam Intermón)
summary: Argues for redesigning the Impuesto sobre el Patrimonio to raise substantially more revenue and restore progressivity among the super-rich, with estimates by Julio López Laborda and Anabel Zárate Marco and by Carmen Durrer.

title: El Impuesto Temporal de Solidaridad de las grandes fortunas y su encaje con el Impuesto sobre el Patrimonio
by: Diego Martínez, Manuel Díaz and Carmen Marín (Fedea)
summary: Sets out the main features of the planned solidarity tax on net wealth above EUR 3 million and analyses how it fits with the regional Impuesto sobre el Patrimonio and what it means for the finances of the autonomous communities, without assessing the tax itself.

title: Three ways Australia can tax wealth better
by: David Richardson and Matt Grudnoff (The Australia Institute)
summary: Recommends an annual 2% wealth tax on net assets above $5 million (family home and superannuation exempt), which it estimates would raise $41 billion a year, alongside an inheritance tax and scrapping the CGT discount.

title: Greens will tax 150 billionaires as part of revenue plan to fund dental into Medicare, GP for free and other cost of living measures
by: Australian Greens
summary: Announces a Parliamentary Budget Office-costed plan under which Australia's 150 billionaires would pay an annual 10% tax on their net wealth, expected to raise $23 billion over the forward estimates and $50 billion over the decade.

title: Matters of Urgency: Cost of Living (tax billionaires), urgency motion by Senator Nick McKim
by: Senator Nick McKim (Australian Greens)
summary: Urgency motion calling on the Government to support the Greens plan to tax Australia's billionaires and use the revenue for cost of living relief; the Greens plan is an annual 10% tax on billionaires' net wealth.
status: Matter of urgency motion put to a Senate division on 11 February 2025 and not passed

title: Wealth taxes and the post-COVID future of the state
by: Jane Andrew, Max Baker, Christine Cooper and Jonathan Tweedie (Critical Perspectives on Accounting)
summary: Argues for a wealth tax on the super-rich, on consequentialist and non-consequentialist grounds of justice, to counter inequalities worsened by COVID-19.

title: Ley 27.605: Aporte Solidario y Extraordinario para ayudar a morigerar los efectos de la pandemia
by: Congreso de la Nación Argentina
summary: Creates a one-off emergency contribution on the assets in Argentina and abroad of residents whose total assets exceed ARS 200 million, on a scale from 2% to 3.5%.
status: Sanctioned by the Congreso on 4 December 2020; published in the Boletín Oficial on 18 December 2020

title: Por un paquete fiscal que termine con la violencia del hambre en la Argentina
by: Claudio Lozano, Agustina Haimovich, Javier Rameri, Ana Rameri, Mariana Rivolta and Eugenia Ventura Flossi (IPyPP)
summary: Proposes a surcharge on the Bienes Personales (personal net wealth) tax on the 50 largest fortunes to raise USD 2 billion, and USD 4 billion if extended to the richest 0.07% of the population.

title: ¿Cuánto podría recaudar el impuesto a las grandes fortunas en América Latina?
by: Sergio Martín Páez and Guillermo Oglietti (CELAG)
summary: Estimates that a 2.5% tax on fortunes above USD 1 million would raise USD 2.4 to 4.7 billion in Argentina (about 30,000 taxpayers) and USD 25 to 50 billion across Latin America.

title: Ley 2277 de 2022: reforma tributaria para la igualdad y la justicia social (impuesto al patrimonio, arts. 35 to 37)
by: Congreso de la República de Colombia (project of the Ministry of Finance under José Antonio Ocampo)
summary: Adds articles 292-3, 294-3 and 295-3 to the Estatuto Tributario, creating a permanent annual wealth tax on net assets of 72,000 UVT or more held on 1 January, with the first 12,000 UVT of a person's home excluded.
status: Ley 2277 de 2022 (Diario Oficial No. 52.247 of 13 December 2022); the Senate's text page was last updated on 15 October 2026

title: Proyecto de Ley 070 de 2020 Cámara: modifica el Decreto Ley 568 de 2020 (impuesto solidario por el COVID-19)
by: Opposition senators and representatives led by Iván Marulanda, Aida Avella and León Fredy Muñoz
summary: The report on the bill describes article 3 as making the wealth tax permanent, with a threshold of 84,253 UVT for individuals and 2,246,749 UVT for legal persons and top marginal rates of 4% and 6%.
status: Report for first debate in the Comisión Tercera of the Cámara (22 September 2020) asks the commission to archive the bill

title: Proyecto de Ley 066 de 2021 Cámara: Ley de Equidad Fiscal
by: Victoria Sandino, Pablo Catatumbo, Aida Avella, Gustavo Petro and others
summary: The positive report for first debate proposes a tax on net wealth for the years 2022 to 2025 among the bill's measures to raise revenue for equity and social wellbeing.
status: Informe de ponencia positiva para primer debate (Gaceta del Congreso 1634, 16 November 2021)

title: A Proposed Wealth Tax on Colombia's 4,700+ Richest Would Raise $1 Billion
by: Omar Ocampo (Institute for Policy Studies)
summary: Estimates that the progressive wealth tax of the incoming government, at 0.25% to 1% on wealth above USD 250,000 to 1 million, would raise about USD 1 billion from the 4,700 or so richest Colombians, and about USD 2.2 billion with added rates of 2% above USD 5 million and 3% above USD 50 million.

title: ¿Cuánto podría recaudar el impuesto a las grandes fortunas en América Latina?
by: Sergio Martín Páez and Guillermo Oglietti (CELAG)
summary: Estimates that a 2.5% tax on fortunes above USD 1 million would raise USD 3.3 to 5.4 billion in Colombia and USD 25 to 50 billion across Latin America.

title: Nota Macroeconómica No. 43: Los impuestos en Colombia: ¿Qué, cómo, cuánto y cuándo reformarlos?
by: Leopoldo Fergusson and Marc Hofstetter (Universidad de los Andes)
summary: Proposes a marginal wealth tax only on net worth above COP 1,000 million, at 0.5%, 1% above COP 3,000 million and 2% above COP 5,000 million, which it estimates would raise close to 1% of GDP.

title: Boletín 13555-07: constitutional reform for a one-time tax on the wealth of certain individuals
by: Deputies Gabriel Ascencio, Karol Cariola, Giorgio Jackson, Daniel Núñez, Luis Rocafull, Alexis Sepúlveda, Alejandra Sepúlveda, Raúl Soto, Camila Vallejo and Esteban Velásquez
summary: Motion to amend the Constitution to set, once only, a tax on the wealth of certain individuals to finance an emergency basic income.
status: Segundo trámite constitucional (the Chamber's page shows the oficio to the revising chamber on 18 May 2021)

title: Hiperfortunas y superricos: ¿por qué tiene sentido un impuesto al patrimonio?
by: Ramón López and Gino Sturla (Revista CEPAL)
summary: Builds a model of the wealth of the richest groups, reviews international experience and the standard objections, and applies a designed net wealth tax to Chile.

title: Impuesto al patrimonio: una propuesta tributaria deficiente
by: Hermann González, Felipe Larraín and Óscar Perelló (Estudios Públicos, CEP)
summary: Argues that a wealth tax can drive capital out and that OECD experience shows low revenue, and that the Chilean proposal would raise far less than its promoters estimate.

title: Wealth Tax Act, 1975 (Number 25 of 1975)
by: Oireachtas
summary: Charges a wealth tax each year at one per cent of the net market value of the taxable wealth of individuals, discretionary trusts and private non-trading companies, from 5 April 1975.
status: Enacted 16 August 1975; section 38 of the Finance Act, 1978 stops the charge for any valuation date on or after 5 April 1978

title: Finance (No. 2) Bill 2023, Report Stage recommendation 3: report on a 2% wealth tax
by: Senator Frances Black, seconded by Senator Paul Gavan
summary: Would oblige the Minister to lay a report on the revenue and distributional impact of a wealth tax of 2 per cent on all households with assets over 20 million euro.
status: Recommendation put and declared lost in Seanad Éireann on 12 December 2023

title: Confronting Wealth Inequality in Ireland
by: Tom McDonnell and Ciarán Nugent (NERI) and Sorley McCaughey, for Oxfam Ireland
summary: Models an annual net wealth tax on the top 1% of the population, with a high threshold of about 3 million euro, and puts the yield of a 1% rate at around 1 billion euro a year (2% about 1.7 billion, 3% about 2.5 billion), as Oxfam Ireland's release states it.

title: Net Wealth Tax for Ireland - Possibilities and Pitfalls (NERI Working Paper 78)
by: Tom McDonnell and Ciarán Nugent (NERI) with Sorley McCaughey
summary: Concludes that a recurrent tax on net household wealth is viable in Ireland if it is simple, has few reliefs and a high threshold reaching about the wealthiest 1%, raising roughly 800 million euro a year.

title: Scenarios and distributional implications of a household wealth tax in Ireland
by: Martina Lawless and Donal Lynch (ESRI; ifo DICE Report 16(2))
summary: Estimates what a household wealth tax could raise in Ireland and how many households would be liable, by applying other European countries' designs and testing combinations of thresholds and asset exemptions.

title: PLP 277/2008: regulates the Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas (art. 153, VII of the Constitution)
by: Chico Alencar, Ivan Valente, Luciana Genro
summary: The oldest of the Tax on Large Fortunes bills before the Câmara, to which later ones are attached.
status: Câmara dos Deputados, situation "Pronta para Pauta" (last entry 2023-06-02, as shown in the Câmara's open data)

title: PLP 26/2011: institutes the Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas (IGF)
by: Amauri Teixeira
summary: Institutes the Tax on Large Fortunes on fortunes above R$ 5,000,000, as the Câmara's summary states.
status: Câmara dos Deputados, situation "Tramitando em Conjunto" (last entry 2019-02-22, as shown in the Câmara's open data)

title: PLP 130/2012: institutes the Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas
by: Amauri Teixeira, Assis Carvalho, Cláudio Puty, Jilmar Tatto, José Guimarães, Paulo Teixeira and 3 other deputies
summary: Institutes the Tax on Large Fortunes provided for in art. 153, VII of the Constitution.
status: Câmara dos Deputados, situation "Tramitando em Conjunto" (last entry 2019-03-19, as shown in the Câmara's open data)

title: PLP 9/2019: institutes the Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas
by: Alessandro Molon, Bira do Pindaré, Camilo Capiberibe, Danilo Cabral, Elias Vaz, João H. Campos and 3 other deputies
summary: Institutes the Tax on Large Fortunes under art. 153, VII of the Constitution.
status: Câmara dos Deputados, situation "Tramitando em Conjunto" (last entry 2020-02-21, as shown in the Câmara's open data)

title: PLP 188/2020: institutes the Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas (IGF)
by: Afonso Florence, Airton Faleiro, Alencar Santana Braga, Alexandre Padilha, Beto Faro, Bohn Gass and 36 other deputies
summary: Institutes the Tax on Large Fortunes provided for in art. 153, VII of the Constitution, in a bill with some 40 deputies as authors (PT group).
status: Câmara dos Deputados, situation "Tramitando em Conjunto" (last entry 2020-12-08, as shown in the Câmara's open data)

title: PLP 193/2020: institutes the Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas
by: Áurea Carolina, David Miranda, Edmilson Rodrigues, Fernanda Melchionna, Glauber Braga, Ivan Valente and 3 other deputies
summary: Institutes the Tax on Large Fortunes under art. 153, VII of the Constitution (PSOL group).
status: Câmara dos Deputados, situation "Tramitando em Conjunto" (last entry 2020-12-08, as shown in the Câmara's open data)

title: PLP 130/2021: institutes the Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas
by: Afonso Florence, Airton Faleiro, Alencar Santana Braga, Alice Portugal, Benedita da Silva, Beto Faro and 49 other deputies
summary: Institutes the Tax on Large Fortunes under art. 153, VII of the Constitution, signed by about 55 deputies.
status: Câmara dos Deputados, situation "Tramitando em Conjunto" (last entry 2022-05-24, as shown in the Câmara's open data)

title: PLP 69/2023: institutes the Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas (IGF)
by: Jorge Goetten
summary: Institutes the Tax on Large Fortunes.
status: Câmara dos Deputados, situation "Aguardando Encaminhamento" (last entry 2023-06-02, as shown in the Câmara's open data)

title: PLP 203/2024: institutes the Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas (IGF)
by: Elisangela Araujo
summary: Institutes the Tax on Large Fortunes provided for in art. 153, VII of the Constitution.
status: Câmara dos Deputados, situation "Aguardando Despacho do Presidente da Câmara dos Deputados (Chancela)" (last entry 2024-11-19, as shown in the Câmara's open data)

title: PLP 5/2026: institutes the Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas
by: Pedro Uczai
summary: Institutes the Tax on Large Fortunes.
status: Câmara dos Deputados, situation "Aguardando Despacho do Presidente da Câmara dos Deputados (Chancela)" (last entry 2026-02-02, as shown in the Câmara's open data)

title: PLS 534/2011: taxation of large fortunes
by: Senator Antonio Carlos Valadares (PSB)
summary: Regulates art. 153, VII of the Constitution: an annual tax on net wealth above R$ 2,500,000 held at 31 December, on Brazilian-born individuals worldwide and on foreigners resident in Brazil for assets there.
status: Senado Federal: "Arquivada ao final da legislatura" (20 December 2018)

title: PLS 315/2015: institutes the Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas
by: Senator Paulo Paim (PT)
summary: Institutes the Tax on Large Fortunes referred to in art. 153, VII of the Constitution.
status: Senado Federal: "Desarquivada" on 16 March 2023, with the Economic Affairs Committee's support secretariat

title: PLS 139/2017: institutes the Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas
by: Senator Vanessa Grazziotin (PCdoB)
summary: Regulates art. 153, VII of the Constitution to institute the Tax on Large Fortunes.
status: Senado Federal: "Arquivada ao final da legislatura" (21 December 2018)

title: PLP 183/2019: institutes the Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas
by: Senator Plínio Valério (PSDB)
summary: Regulates art. 153, VII of the Constitution to institute the Tax on Large Fortunes.
status: Senado Federal: "Aguardando designação do relator" (2 February 2023)

title: PLP 38/2020: Extraordinary Tax on Large Fortunes during the public calamity
by: Senator Reguffe (PODE)
summary: Institutes an extraordinary tax on large fortunes for the duration of the public calamity declared for covid-19.
status: Senado Federal: "Arquivada ao final da legislatura" (21 December 2022)

title: PLP 50/2020: tax on large fortunes and compulsory loan for covid-19 social protection
by: Senator Eliziane Gama (Cidadania)
summary: Institutes a tax on large fortunes and a compulsory loan to finance social protection needs arising from covid-19.
status: Senado Federal: "Matéria com a relatoria" (19 April 2023)

title: PLP 101/2021: Extraordinary Contribution on Large Fortunes
by: Senator Randolfe Rodrigues (Rede)
summary: Institutes an extraordinary contribution on large fortunes to ease the effects of the covid-19 pandemic.
status: Senado Federal: "Aguardando designação do relator" (9 May 2023)

title: PLP 125/2021: institutes the Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas
by: Senator Jorge Kajuru (PODE)
summary: Regulates art. 153, VII of the Constitution to institute the Tax on Large Fortunes.
status: Senado Federal: "Aguardando designação do relator" (9 May 2023)

title: Tributar os super-ricos para reconstruir o país (executive report)
by: Fenafisco, Anfip, Instituto Justiça Fiscal and Auditores Fiscais pela Democracia
summary: Eight tax-law proposals that include regulating the Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas (rates of 0.5%, 1% and 1.5%, raised for five years to 1%, 2% and 3%), which it estimates at R$ 40 billion of a total R$ 292 billion a year, falling on the richest 0.3%.

title: Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas: o recente debate internacional e a situação no Brasil (One Pager 378)
by: Pedro Carvalho Jr. (Ipea) and Luana Passos (UFF)
summary: Reviews the recent international debate on taxing large fortunes and the situation of the Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas, still unregulated in Brazil since the 1988 Constitution.

title: Antrag 17/2944: Auswege aus der Krise: Steuerpolitische Gerechtigkeit und Handlungsfähigkeit des Staates wiederherstellen
by: Fraktion Die Linke (Barbara Höll, Axel Troost, Sahra Wagenknecht and others)
summary: Among its demands, asks the government to bring back the wealth tax as a millionaires' tax, at 5% of net wealth above an allowance of 1,000,000 euro.
status: Motion tabled in the Bundestag (Drucksache 17/2944); the 17th Bundestag has since ended

title: Antrag 17/8792: Wer Schulden bremsen will, muss Millionäre besteuern
by: Fraktion Die Linke (Barbara Höll, Axel Troost, Sahra Wagenknecht and others)
summary: Asks the government for a bill that brings back the wealth tax as a millionaires' tax: 5% on net wealth above 1,000,000 euro.
status: Debated on 23 March 2012 and referred to committees (Bundestag text archive); no vote shown there. The 17th Bundestag has since ended

title: Gesetzentwurf 17/10770: Entwurf eines Gesetzes zur Erhebung einer Vermögensabgabe
by: Fraktion Bündnis 90/Die Grünen (Lisa Paus, Kerstin Andreae, Britta Haßelmann and others)
summary: Bill for a one-off wealth levy on the richest, modelled on the post-war Lastenausgleich, to reduce the public debt caused by the financial crisis.
status: Roll call in the Bundestag on 27 June 2013: 66 yes, 318 no, 195 abstentions (official name list)

title: Antrag 17/10778: Reichtum umFAIRteilen – in Deutschland und Europa
by: Fraktion Die Linke (Alexander Ulrich, Gregor Gysi, Sahra Wagenknecht and others)
summary: Among its demands, asks the government to work at EU level for a Europe-wide coordinated wealth levy (Vermögensabgabe).
status: Motion tabled in the Bundestag (Drucksache 17/10778); the 17th Bundestag has since ended

title: Antrag 19/94: Reichtum gerechter verteilen – Vermögensteuer als Millionärsteuer wieder erheben
by: Fraktion Die Linke (Klaus Ernst, Fabio De Masi, Bernd Riexinger and others)
summary: Asks the government for a bill that brings back the wealth tax as a millionaires' tax: 5% above 1 million euro, with a higher allowance of 5 million euro for business assets.
status: Motion tabled in the Bundestag (Drucksache 19/94); the 19th Bundestag has since ended

title: Antrag 19/28908: Einmalige Vermögensabgabe für Milliardäre und Multimillionäre
by: Fraktion Die Linke (Fabio De Masi, Stefan Liebich, Klaus Ernst and others)
summary: Asks the government for a one-off wealth levy under Article 106(1) no. 5 of the Basic Law, aimed at no more than the richest 0.7% of adults and at least 300 billion euro.
status: Motion tabled in the Bundestag (Drucksache 19/28908); the 19th Bundestag has since ended

title: Antrag 20/4307: Einmalige Vermögensabgabe für Multimillionäre und Milliardäre
by: Fraktion Die Linke (Christian Görke, Gesine Lötzsch, Klaus Ernst and others)
summary: Asks the government for a bill creating a one-off wealth levy on multimillionaires and billionaires under Article 106(1) no. 5 of the Basic Law, on the model of the Lastenausgleich.
status: Rejected by the Bundestag on 10 November 2022 in a named vote: 36 yes, 649 no (Bundestag text archive)

title: Antrag 21/8267: 500-Millionen-Steuer – Extremvermögen fairer beteiligen
by: Fraktion Bündnis 90/Die Grünen (Karoline Otte, Katharina Beck, Katharina Dröge and others)
summary: Asks the government to introduce a tax on net wealth above an allowance of 500 million euro, at 2% rising to 3% above 1 billion and 4% above 10 billion euro.
status: Motion tabled in the Bundestag (Drucksache 21/8267)

title: Antrag 19/1952: Vermögensteuer wieder einführen – Reiche müssen ihren fairen Beitrag leisten!
by: Fraktion Die Linke (Abgeordnetenhaus von Berlin)
summary: Asks the Berlin Senate to start a Bundesrat initiative to bring back the wealth tax and to commission a legal opinion on whether the Land now has the power to do so.
status: Committees recommended rejection (Drucksache 19/2364, 3 April 2025: Ausschuss für Bundes- und Europaangelegenheiten 12 March, Hauptausschuss 2 April; CDU, SPD and AfD against Greens and Linke); no plenary decision seen

title: Antrag 7/845: Wiederbelebung der Vermögensteuer als Teil einer gerechten Steuerpolitik
by: Fraktion Die Linke (Landtag von Sachsen-Anhalt)
summary: Asks the state government to work for a Bundesrat initiative to bring back the wealth tax in Germany.
status: Motion tabled in the Landtag of Saxony-Anhalt (Drucksache 7/845); the 7th term has since ended

title: Antrag 19/4497: Wiederbelebung der Vermögensteuer als Teil einer gerechten Steuerpolitik
by: Fraktion Die Linke (Hessischer Landtag)
summary: Asks the state government to work for a Bundesrat initiative to bring back the wealth tax in Germany.
status: Motion tabled in the Hessian Landtag (Drucksache 19/4497); the 19th term has since ended

title: Vermögensteuer: Erhebliches Aufkommenspotential trotz erwartbarer Ausweichreaktionen (DIW Wochenbericht 42/2012)
by: Stefan Bach and Martin Beznoska (DIW Berlin)
summary: Models a 1% wealth tax with a personal allowance of 2 million euro and finds it would still raise about 11.6 billion euro a year after avoidance responses.

title: Hohes Aufkommenspotential bei Wiedererhebung der Vermögensteuer (DIW Wochenbericht 4/2016)
by: Stefan Bach and Andreas Thiemann (DIW Berlin)
summary: Uses a microsimulation model to estimate that a reinstated wealth tax could raise ten to twenty billion euro a year even with high allowances, though avoidance could cut that noticeably.

title: Der grundgesetzliche Rahmen für die Wiedereinführung einer Vermögensteuer (HBS Working Paper 266)
by: Alexander Thiele (Hans-Böckler-Stiftung)
summary: A legal opinion that concludes the Basic Law does not stand in the way of reintroducing a wealth tax.

title: Vedtak om skatt av inntekt og formue mv. for inntektsåret 2026 (Stortingets skattevedtak, Vedtak 212)
by: Stortinget (Prop. 1 LS and Innst. 3 S, 2025–2026)
status: Vedtak 212 in the Storting's decisions on Skatter og avgifter 2026 (Prop. 1 LS, Innst. 3 S, 2025–2026); the page shows no decision date
summary: The annual decision that sets Norway's net wealth tax for income year 2026: a state rate of 0.65% above NOK 1.9 million (0.75% above NOK 21.5 million), a municipal rate of at most 0.35%, and 1.0% and 1.1% for taxpayers under skatteloven § 2-3 first paragraph letters k to n.

title: NOU 2022: 20 Et helhetlig skattesystem
by: Skatteutvalget (chair Ragnar Torvik), for the Ministry of Finance
summary: The expert committee's majority keeps a net wealth tax but would cut its revenue by NOK 8.4 billion (a much higher threshold, lower rates, a wider base without valuation discounts) and replace part of it with an inheritance tax; a minority wants a still smaller wealth tax.

title: Wealth Taxation and Household Saving: Evidence from Assessment Discontinuities in Norway
by: Marius A. K. Ring (University of Texas at Austin)
summary: Uses geographic discontinuities in Norway's annual net wealth tax and third-party saving data to find that each krone of wealth tax raises annual net financial saving by 3.76 kroner, mostly through higher labour earnings.

title: Motie-Alkaya (36 418, nr. 74): mondiale minimumvermogensbelasting voor miljardairs
by: Mahir Alkaya (SP)
status: Described as adopted ("de aangenomen motie van het lid Alkaya") in the follow-up motion of 4 April 2024 (25 087, nr. 330); the vote itself was not read
summary: Asks the government to form a lead group of OECD countries that actively campaigns for a global minimum wealth tax on billionaires, citing the EU Tax Observatory's Global Tax Evasion Report.

title: Motie-Van der Lee (36 418, nr. 76): inzet voor een wereldwijde miljardairsbelasting
by: Tom van der Lee (GroenLinks-PvdA)
status: Adopted by show of hands on the Tweede Kamer's page (132 of 150 seats in favour)
summary: Asks the government to push in international forums for a global billionaire tax and to take the initiative with like-minded countries, for example with a white paper.

title: Motie-De Jong c.s. (36 202, nr. 102): onderzoek naar een miljonairsbelasting
by: Romke de Jong (D66) and co-signatories
status: Adopted by show of hands on the Tweede Kamer's page
summary: Asks the government to examine how a millionaire tax could be designed, for example a 1% wealth tax on box 3 assets above €1 million, so that workable scenarios exist for coalition talks.

title: Proposta di legge di iniziativa popolare "Imposta grandi patrimoni" (campagna 1%Equo)
by: Comitato 1%Equo, promoted by Rifondazione Comunista with economists and researchers (first signatory Maurizio Acerbo)
status: Presented to the Corte di Cassazione on 7 May 2026 under art. 71 of the Constitution; signature collection runs 15 May to 15 November 2026 and the bill has no number in Parliament (promoters' text and Pagella Politica)
summary: An annual personal tax on net wealth above €2 million, excluding the main home, at 1% to €5 million, 1.7% to €8 million, 2.1% to €20 million and 3.5% above, with IMU, IVIE and IVAFE deducted.

title: L'agenda TaxTheRich per l'Italia: Manifesto degli economisti e delle economiste italiani/e
by: 134 Italian economists, drafted by Demetrio Guzzardi, Elisa Palagi and Andrea Roventini (Sant'Anna School), presented with Oxfam Italia
summary: Asks for a progressive tax on the richest 0.1% of citizens, with net wealth above €5.4 million, in line with the European Citizens' Initiative, within a year, together with higher inheritance tax and more top income-tax brackets.

title: Tackling the regressivity of the Italian tax system: An optimal taxation framework with heterogeneous returns to capital
by: Matteo Dalle Luche, Demetrio Guzzardi, Elisa Palagi, Andrea Roventini and Alessandro Santoro (World Inequality Lab WP 2024/23)
summary: Using ECB distributional wealth accounts, finds the Italian tax system regressive over the top 7% and estimates the revenue and inequality effects of higher optimal rates on capital income or of a progressive wealth tax.

title: 富裕税法 (Wealth Tax Act, Law No. 174 of 1950)
by: The Diet of Japan, after the 1949 Shoup recommendations
status: Promulgated 11 May 1950; repealed with effect from 1 August 1953 by Law No. 164 of 1953 (Nagoya University law database)
summary: Japan's only permanent net wealth tax: a yearly progressive tax on net worth over ¥5 million at 0.5%, rising to 1% above ¥10 million, 2% above ¥20 million and 3% above ¥50 million.

title: 「富裕税法」再導入論
by: Masato Kikuya (菊谷正人), Keieishirin vol. 53 no. 2 (Hosei University)
summary: Compares the one-off 1946 property tax law with the 1950 wealth tax law and proposes reintroducing a general net wealth tax, with concrete rules on taxable persons and revaluation of property.

title: 부유세와 종합부동산세: 부유세의 조세정책적 의미 (Wealth tax and the comprehensive real estate tax)
by: Korea Institute of Public Finance (KIPF)
summary: Examines proposals for a net wealth tax in Korea, the Swedish and French experience, the comprehensive real estate tax as a wealth tax, and the revenue and distribution effects of alternative designs.

title: 순부유세 도입 시 문제점에 관한 연구 (The Study on the Introduction of the Net Wealth Tax in Korea)
by: Young Hoon Kim, Park Sung Ook and Juneq Lee (Kyung Hee University), 회계저널 vol. 23 no. 5
summary: Argues that a net wealth tax would bring high administration costs, constitutional doubts about valuing unrealised gains and joint assessment of spouses, and double taxation, and recommends fixing the capital gains tax first.

title: 감세정국에서 부유세 도입을 말하다 (forum proceedings)
by: Keynote by Jung Se-eun (Chungnam National University) with discussants from the Labour, Green and Justice parties and civil society; posted by the Labour Party
summary: Proceedings of a forum on introducing a wealth tax amid tax cuts, with a keynote on the issues in creating one and six discussant papers, one of which argues for strengthening asset taxes instead.

title: Que reforma y adiciona diversas disposiciones de la Ley del Impuesto sobre la Renta, en materia de impuesto a las grandes fortunas
by: Dip. José Luis Sánchez González (Partido del Trabajo)
summary: Initiative in the Chamber of Deputies to add to the income tax law a progressive annual tax on the net wealth of individuals above 100 million pesos, with rates of 1.5%, 2.5% and 3.5%.
status: Initiative presented to the Chamber of Deputies and published in the Gaceta Parlamentaria of 3 March 2026 (as listed on the sponsor's page); no committee report or vote seen

title: Proyecto de Ley 5163/2020-CR: Ley de Impuesto a las Grandes Fortunas
by: Rocío Silva Santisteban and Mirtha Vásquez (Frente Amplio)
summary: Bill to create an annual tax on the net personal wealth of resident individuals above 400 tax units (UIT), on real estate, vehicles, shares, deposits and valuables, to fund the fight against COVID-19.
status: Received by Congress on 12 May 2020; no committee report or vote found, and the 2020-2021 Congress has ended

title: Proyecto de Ley 06615/2020-CR: Ley que crea el Impuesto de Solidaridad sobre la Fortuna
by: Betto Barrionuevo Romero and other members of the Somos Perú group
summary: Bill to create a progressive tax on the net wealth of individuals, conjugal partnerships and intestate estates above 250 tax units (UIT).
status: Sent to the Economy, Banking, Finance and Financial Intelligence Committee on 9 November 2020 and marked 'en comisión' on 10 November 2020; no vote found, and the 2020-2021 Congress has ended

title: Impuestos a la Riqueza o al Patrimonio de las Personas Físicas con especial mención a América Latina y El Caribe
by: Juan Carlos Benítez and Fernando Velayos (CIAT)
summary: CIAT working paper on the design, efficiency and legal issues of taxes on the net wealth of individuals, with simulations of such a tax for selected Latin American countries including Peru.

title: Koncepcja globalnego podatku majątkowego
by: Grzegorz Malinowski and Jacek Tomkiewicz
summary: Article in Nierówności Społeczne a Wzrost Gospodarczy arguing for a global progressive tax on wealth, preceded by a register of assets, to reduce wealth inequality and raise public revenue.

title: Czy podatek majątkowy może uzdrowić finanse publiczne i zmniejszyć nierówności majątkowe w Polsce?
by: Marcin Wroński (Instytut Badań Strukturalnych)
summary: IBS Policy Paper estimating that a tax on net household wealth in Poland would raise 5-9 billion zloty (0.2-0.4% of GDP) and concluding that its effect on wealth inequality would be small and its costs high.

title: Jak multimilionerzy mogą pomóc w ratowaniu klimatu?
by: Partia Razem
summary: Party position proposing a progressive wealth tax with a 10 million zloty exemption and rates from 1% to 8%, a national wealth register and an exit tax, estimated to raise about 10 billion zloty a year.

title: Towards Tax Justice and Wealth Redistribution in India: Proposals based on latest inequality estimates
by: Nitin Kumar Bharti, Lucas Chancel, Thomas Piketty and Anmol Somanchi (World Inequality Lab)
summary: Issue brief that costs a baseline 2% annual tax on net wealth above 10 crore rupees plus a 33% inheritance tax at about 2.7% of GDP, falling on 0.04% of adults.

title: Wealth Tracker India 2026: Tax the Top, Close the Gap
by: Centre for Financial Accountability and the Tax the Top campaign
summary: Campaign report on the wealth of 1,688 Indians above 1,000 crore rupees that calls for a progressive 2% to 6% wealth tax plus a one-third inheritance tax, which it puts at 10.63 lakh crore rupees a year.

title: A Wealth Tax for South Africa
by: Aroop Chatterjee, Léo Czajka and Amory Gethin (World Inequality Lab Working Paper 2021/02)
summary: Working paper that designs a progressive annual wealth tax for South Africa's richest and estimates, under different assumptions about evasion, that it could raise 1.5% to 3.5% of GDP.

title: Taxing the Rich: Nigerian Fair Tax Monitor Thematic Report
by: CISLAC, Oxfam in Nigeria and Tax Justice Network Africa, with Oxfam Novib
summary: Report on how Nigeria taxes its high-net-worth individuals that recommends a progressive net wealth tax (1% from 1 million dollars, 2% from 5 million, 5% from 50 million) and cites an estimate of over 6 billion dollars a year.

title: House Bill No. 10253: An Act imposing a 'Super-Rich Tax' on individuals with net value assets exceeding one billion pesos
by: Reps. Ferdinand Gaite, Carlos Zarate, Eufemia Cullamat, France Castro, Arlene Brosas and Sarah Jane Elago (Makabayan bloc)
summary: Proposes a yearly tax of 1% on wealth above 1 billion pesos, 2% above 2 billion and 3% above 3 billion, amending the National Internal Revenue Code.
status: Filed 20 September 2021, Eighteenth Congress, Third Regular Session (date stamp on the House text); the Eighteenth Congress ended in June 2022

title: House Bill No. 4304: An Act imposing Solidarity Contribution on the most affluent Filipinos for the benefit of public health and climate change resiliency
by: Reps. Percival Cendaña, Jose Manuel Diokno, Dadah Kiram Ismula (Akbayan) and Kaka Bag-ao
summary: Imposes a solidarity contribution on the net worth (assets less liabilities) of the most affluent individuals, with revenue earmarked for universal health care and climate resilience.
status: Filed 3 September 2025, Twentieth Congress, First Regular Session (date stamp on the House text); no later action seen

title: House Bill No. 8123: An Act imposing a 'Billionaire Wealth Tax' on individuals
by: Reps. Antonio Tinio, Sarah Jane Elago and Renee Louise Co (Makabayan bloc)
summary: Proposes an annual tax of 1% on wealth above 1 billion pesos, 2% above 2 billion and 3% above 3 billion on individual billionaires.
status: Filed 26 February 2026, Twentieth Congress, First Regular Session (date stamp on the House text); no later action seen

title: House Bill No. 9274: An Act imposing an 'Ultra-Wealth Tax' on individuals with net assets exceeding one billion pesos
by: Rep. Leila M. de Lima
summary: Imposes an annual Ultra-Wealth Tax of 1% on wealth above 1 billion pesos, 2% above 2 billion and 3% above 3 billion, with revenue for health, education, social protection and housing.
status: Filed 18 May 2026, Twentieth Congress, First Regular Session (date stamp on the House text); no later action seen

title: Inequality, Tax Justice and the Philippine Wealth Tax Campaign
by: Eduardo C. Tadem (UP Center for Integrative and Development Studies, Program on Alternative Development)
summary: Monograph that sets out the case for a Philippine wealth tax and traces the civil-society and labour campaign for it.

title: Tax the super-rich
by: IBON Foundation
summary: IBON estimates that a tax of 1% on wealth above 1 billion pesos, 2% above 2 billion and 3% above 3 billion would raise at least 502 billion pesos a year from about 3,000 billionaires.
